patients.summary: Retired shipyard worker, 90 pack-year former smoker with asbestos exposure, who joins in 2023 for a chronic productive cough; bronchiectasis and asbestosis are found, then extensive-stage small cell lung cancer presenting with hypercalcemia. Chemoimmunotherapy, malignant pleural and pericardial effusions, a port infection, SIADH and a central airway mass follow, mostly seen through sparse outside notes.

documents.title: New Patient Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer his primary care here; his old doctor retired this spring and he hasn't connected with whoever took over. Medicare. Booked new patient appt 6/13 at 9:00. Release signed by fax for his old office notes and med list. Told him to bring his pill bottles.

events.reason: records from prior primary care office

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Faxed packet, 9 pages, from his previous family practice.

Medication list: atorvastatin 40 mg daily; aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Problem list: hyperlipidemia; tobacco use, quit 2021; occupational asbestos exposure (shipyard).

April 2023 sick visit: fever, productive cough, crackles at the right base; treated as community-acquired pneumonia with an oral antibiotic course, improved at phone follow-up. Not admitted.

Older visits note repeated winter chest infections treated with antibiotics. No colonoscopy on file.

Scanned to chart.

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: years of daily purulent sputum, frequent chest infections, clubbing

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65M establishing care. Previous PCP retired; records from that office reviewed.

Main issue is his cough. Every morning he brings up a lot of thick yellow-green phlegm, often with a bad smell, mostly in the first hour after he gets up. Says he has had a chest infection that needed antibiotics most years for about five years; the last one in April was called pneumonia and treated at home with pills. Feels back to his usual now. No fevers, sweats or weight change.

PMH: high cholesterol on atorvastatin. Took aspirin on old doctor's advice, brother has heart disease.
Meds: atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: none to medicines.
Family: father died of lung cancer at 68, smoked heavily. Mother had emphysema. Brother with coronary disease.
Social: married, lives with wife. Thirty years at the naval shipyard, retired at 55; worked around insulation and lagging, asbestos exposure for years. Smoked about two packs a day for roughly 45 years (90 pk-yr), finally quit in 2021 after several tries. A beer once or twice a month. Walks now and then.

Exam: BP and vitals as charted. Comfortable, no distress. Clubbing of the fingers. Lungs with scattered rhonchi over both bases, clear after cough in part, no wheeze. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft. No edema.

A/P
1. Chronic productive cough with recurrent infections, clubbing, heavy smoking and asbestos history. Needs a pulmonary evaluation and CT. Referral to pulmonology placed.
2. Hyperlipidemia: continue atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
3. Former smoker, asbestos exposure: pulmonology will steer imaging.
4. Health maintenance: PCV20 and Tdap today. Hep C and HIV screening with labs. CMP, CBC, lipids.
RTC early September for his wellness visit.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Casey, everything from Tuesday came back fine: kidney and liver tests, blood count, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Your cholesterol numbers look good on the atorvastatin, so no change. Pulmonology should call you to set up the visit; let us know if you don't hear in two weeks.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Date of visit 7/17/2023. Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Casey.

Reason: daily purulent sputum.
He raises a large volume of foul, yellow-green sputum each morning, heaviest right after waking. About five years of recurrent respiratory infections, each needing antibiotics. No weight loss, fevers or night sweats.

History: hyperlipidemia. Ex-smoker, 90 pack-years, quit 2021. Shipyard work with asbestos exposure. Meds atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. NKDA.

Exam: digital clubbing. Scattered rhonchi over both lung bases. No wheeze.

CT chest 7/11/2023 (reviewed): thick-walled, dilated bronchi in both lower lobes with mucus plugging and cystic change.

Impression: bronchiectasis, bilateral lower lobes.

Plan: daily airway clearance with an oscillating PEP device, twice a day, technique taught today. Treat flares with antibiotics early. Will see him again in October.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Refill: atorvastatin
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy e-request for atorvastatin 40 mg #90. Last lipids 6/13 fine. Sent 90 days, 1 refill, per protocol.

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

documents.title: Welcome to Medicare Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preventive visit. 65-year-old man, seen by pulmonology in July for his cough, told he has bronchiectasis; doing the flutter device most mornings. Nothing new bothering him today.

Meds: atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. Allergies none.
Function: independent, drives, no falls. Hearing and vision okay for him. PHQ-2 negative.

Vitals in normal range. Exam: well appearing. Clubbing as before. Chest with a few coarse sounds at the bases. Heart regular. Abdomen benign. Skin unremarkable.

Counseling: we talked about what is most likely to threaten his health over the coming years. With 90 pack-years, decades of asbestos and his father's lung cancer, lung cancer is the big one, more than his heart. Pulmonology has a CT planned for October, which will cover the screening question, so I am not ordering a separate low-dose CT now. He knows to call for coughing up blood, weight loss or new chest pain.

Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2 to 6 months. Flu/COVID/RSV when supplies are in, nurse visit.
Advance directive packet given.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu L deltoid, updated COVID R deltoid, RSV L deltoid lower site. Screening questions negative. Waited 15 min, no reaction. VIS sheets given.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group, follow-up 10/10/2023.

Back after the July consult; his PCP saw him in September. Ongoing cough, and over the last couple of months he gets winded sooner on hills and stairs. No chest pain, no blood in the sputum, weight steady.

Exam: fine inspiratory crackles at both bases. Clubbing.

Chest x-ray: interstitial fibrotic change with pleural plaques.
HRCT 10/6/2023: diffuse subpleural reticulation with honeycombing. Separately, soft tissue fullness at the right hilum, not well characterized on a non-contrast study; contrast-enhanced CT advised.
PFTs: restrictive pattern.

Impression:
1. Asbestosis with pleural plaques, on top of his known lower-lobe bronchiectasis.
2. Right hilar abnormality, suspicious for a malignancy given his history.

Plan: we spent time on what to expect over the long term: the fibrosis tends to progress slowly, and with his asbestos and smoking history his risks of lung cancer and of mesothelioma are both well above average. Contrast CT chest ordered, first opening is late November. Continue airway clearance.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Pulmonology Letter Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt after reading the pulm note. Went over the scarring from asbestos, and that the CT also showed something at the right side of the chest center that needs a dye CT to sort out. He had heard the same from pulm and is booked for late November. Asked if it could go sooner; he would rather keep the date, his wife has a procedure the week before. Offered to push for an earlier slot anyway, he declined. Added to problem list. Call if any blood in sputum, weight loss, or he feels worse.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of lung
conditions.note: small cell carcinoma, right hilar, extensive stage, stage IV

procedures.procedure: Percutaneous needle biopsy of lung, CT-guided

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 11/18/2023.
CC: confused, tired, constipated x several days, per wife.
Pt slow to answer, lethargic. Dry mucous membranes, mildly dry. Reflexes sluggish, cannot keep attention on serial tasks. Nonfocal otherwise.
Ca 13.9, phos 1.9, PTH low (9).
CXR: 4.5 cm R hilar mass.
Imp: hypercalcemia, low PTH, hilar mass, concern for malignancy. IV NS started. Admit to medicine.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 11/18/2023, discharged 11/24/2023.
Dx: hypercalcemia due to malignancy; small cell lung cancer, extensive stage (stage IV) with malignant right pleural effusion.

Course: IV saline and zoledronic acid 4 mg IV x1; mental status cleared by day 3. Contrast CT chest: right hilar mass, small right effusion. CT abd/pelvis and MRI brain without metastatic disease. CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy 11/21: small cell carcinoma. Diagnostic right thoracentesis 11/22: cytology positive for malignant cells. Ca 10.2 on day of discharge.

Discharge meds: atorvastatin 40 daily, aspirin 81 daily (unchanged).
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: oncology consult arranged for early December; PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with his wife, 4 days after discharge. Discharge summary reviewed (received 11/27).

He came in with confusion and constipation; calcium was 13.9 and a 4.5 cm right hilar mass was found. Biopsy showed small cell carcinoma, and the fluid around the right lung had cancer cells, so it is extensive stage. He got fluids and a dose of zoledronic acid and cleared quickly.

Today he is sharp, oriented, bowels moving. Some fatigue. Wife is taking notes and doing the driving.

Exam: alert, appropriate. Lungs: crackles at bases as before, slightly reduced sounds at R base. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. Small cell lung cancer, extensive stage, malignant R pleural effusion. Oncology consult 12/4. We talked about how treatment usually goes and that I'll stay involved. They asked good questions; both understandably shaken.
2. Hypercalcemia: resolved. BMP today. Call for confusion, constipation, vomiting.
3. Bronchiectasis, asbestosis: keep up airway clearance.
4. HLD: continue atorvastatin, aspirin.
Will touch base after he meets oncology.

documents.title: Update from wife
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is Bill's wife writing for him. He started treatment on the 11th: carboplatin and etoposide with atezolizumab, every three weeks. The cancer doctor said four rounds then the immune drug alone. He's tired but managing. Just wanted you to know. Do we still need the second shingles shot?

documents.title: Re: Update from wife
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, I'm glad the first round went okay. Let's hold the second shingles shot until his counts settle; we can give it at his spring visit. Message any time.

documents.title: Refill: atorvastatin
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Atorvastatin 40 mg, 90-day supply requested by pharmacy. Approved, 1 refill. Aspirin is OTC, he buys it himself.

documents.title: Oncology Treatment Summary
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group, summary to PCP.
Dx: small cell lung cancer, extensive stage, malignant R pleural effusion (11/2023).
Treatment: carboplatin/etoposide plus atezolizumab, cycle 1 12/11/2023, 4 cycles completed 3/2024. Now on atezolizumab every 4 weeks as maintenance.
Next restaging in about 3 months.
Allergies: NKDA. Other meds: atorvastatin, aspirin.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Check-in. Finished four rounds of chemo with immunotherapy in March, now getting atezolizumab monthly at the cancer center. Energy coming back slowly, eating fine, lost a few pounds over the winter. Still brings up sputum in the mornings, less on most days; doing the PEP device.

Meds: atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, plus atezolizumab via oncology.

Exam: thin but well. Clubbing. Crackles at both bases, unchanged. Heart regular, no edema.

A/P
1. ES-SCLC on maintenance immunotherapy, per oncology summary of 4/8.
2. Bronchiectasis, asbestosis: stable.
3. HLD: continue statin.
4. Shingrix #2 today, ok with oncology.
Follow up in the summer, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Wife called, infusion got moved to tomorrow and they can't do both. Cancelled 7/23. She'll call back to rebook after his scans.

reports.text: Large circumferential pericardial effusion. Right ventricular diastolic collapse and exaggerated respiratory variation in mitral inflow, consistent with tamponade physiology. Left ventricular systolic function normal by visual estimate. No significant valvular disease.
reports.conclusion: Large pericardial effusion with echocardiographic evidence of cardiac tamponade.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 9/14/2024.
SCLC, extensive stage, recurrent R pleural effusion, tapped at the cancer center about a week ago with relief; now short of breath again, coughing, chest pain worse lying flat. No injury.
BP 100/60, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 92% RA.
JVP up, heart sounds muffled.
Bedside then formal echo: large pericardial effusion, tamponade.
Pericardiocentesis by cardiology, fluid sent; cytology malignant cells.
Admitted. NKDA.
Addendum: R effusion reaccumulated; talc pleurodesis done 9/18 before discharge 9/20.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife after a 6-day stay. Only the brief ED note has come over; history from them.

Timeline per pt: fluid taken off the R lung at the cancer center on 9/6, felt better for a few days, then breathless, coughing, chest pain lying down. ED found a large fluid collection around the heart pressing on it; drained, fluid had cancer cells. While in, the R lung fluid came back and they did a talc procedure to seal it on 9/18.

Now: breathing much better, lying flat again, no chest pain, walking the house without stopping.

Exam: vitals as charted, not tachycardic today. Heart sounds normal, no rub. Reduced sounds R base, crackles both bases as before. No JVD. No edema.

A/P
1. Malignant pericardial effusion with tamponade, drained. Tamponade resolved. Oncology plans to continue atezolizumab, repeat echo per them.
2. Recurrent malignant R pleural effusion, s/p pleurodesis.
3. Return precautions reviewed: breathlessness, chest pain, lightheadedness -> ED.
Requested full discharge summary from hospital.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high dose) R arm, COVID L arm. Oncology ok'd, timed between infusions. Tolerated. Observed 15 min.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Feels he has been holding steady since September. Monthly atezolizumab continues. Morning sputum unchanged. No falls, managing stairs at home slowly. Wife handles appointments.

PHQ-2: 1, feels down some days, no loss of interest; declines counseling for now.
Health care proxy: wife; MOLST discussion started, he wants to think it over with his oncologist.

Vitals stable. Weight 77. Exam: chest as before, heart regular, no edema.

Plan: meds unchanged (atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81). Vaccines up to date this season. Follow up in spring.

documents.title: Scan results and port
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Writing for Bill again. His February scans showed the cancer is growing, so they stopped the atezolizumab. He had a port put in on Tuesday the 25th. He goes in on March 8 to start carboplatin and etoposide again, they want to keep him in the hospital for the first round. No changes to his other pills.

documents.title: Re: Scan results and port
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update. Sorry the scans weren't better news. Keep the port site clean and dry for now, and call oncology or us for fever, redness or swelling there. I'll check in after his stay.

results.text: Coagulase-negative staphylococci, port and peripheral sets

reports.text: Portable AP view. Right chest port with catheter tip at the cavoatrial junction. No focal infiltrate or consolidation. Post-pleurodesis change at the right base. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: Oncology Discharge Summary
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Inpatient oncology, admitted 3/8/2025, discharged 3/18/2025. Age 67.
Admitted for C1 carboplatin/etoposide (rechallenge) via port placed 2/25.
HD3: T 38.9, rigors, dyspnea. BP 110/70, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA. No cough, sputum or urinary sx. Port site mildly tender, no erythema or drainage. Lungs clear.
WBC 12.0, Hgb 10.2, plt 250. UA neg. CXR no infiltrate.
Blood cx port + peripheral: coag-negative staph. Dx catheter-related bloodstream infection.
Vancomycin IV, 14-day course with antibiotic lock, port retained. Repeat cx no growth.
Chemo completed. Cycles 2-4 outpatient.
NKDA. Home meds unchanged: atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One week out from a 10-day oncology admission. Discharge summary in.

Went in for the first round of carboplatin/etoposide again after progression in Feb. Day 3 he spiked to 38.9 with shaking chills; cultures from the new port and his arm grew coag-negative staph. Port kept, vancomycin 2 weeks with lock, last cultures clean. Antibiotic finished yesterday.

Today: no fevers at home, port site not sore, appetite fair. Next cycle on the 31st.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Port R upper chest, healed incision, no redness or tenderness. Lungs with bibasilar crackles, unchanged. Heart regular. No edema.

CBC today.

A/P
1. Port infection, treated; resolved.
2. ES-SCLC, second-line carbo/etoposide.
3. Anemia from chemo, following with oncology.
4. HLD: continue atorvastatin, aspirin.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: His white count is back to normal and the hemoglobin is 10.6, a bit better than in the hospital. That's the chemo's effect and oncology is watching it too. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Refill: atorvastatin
documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx renewal atorvastatin 40 mg #90 with 3 refills. Approved by PCP.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt and wife on the tablet from their kitchen, ID verified.
Fourth and last round of the carbo/etoposide is next week. Tired for a few days after each one, then recovers. No fevers since March. Cough and morning sputum about the same. Port fine.
Meds: atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81.
Observed: speaking full sentences, no distress, color good.
Plan: no changes. Oncology restaging after this round. Office visit this fall with the flu shot.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu HD L deltoid, COVID R deltoid. Wife says scans in late August showed growth again and he started lurbinectedin every 3 weeks on 9/5; next dose 10/17. Updated med list note for PCP. Tolerated shots, observed 15 min.

conditions.label: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 11/16/2025. 68M, ES-SCLC, prior malignant pleural effusion, earlier admission for hypercalcemia with confusion.
Wife: 3 days of increasing confusion, sleepy; drinking his usual amount, eating little. Last chemo about a month ago.
Vitals WNL. Oriented to self only. Euvolemic, turgor normal, no edema. Foley placed for strict I/O.
Na 119, serum osm 252, urine osm 470, urine Na 54. TSH and AM cortisol normal.
Imp: SIADH, paraneoplastic.
Admitted: fluid restriction, cautious 3% saline in step-down, then salt tabs 1 g TID and 1.2 L/day restriction. Na 128 at discharge 11/20. Foley out day 2.
NKDA. Discharge meds add sodium chloride 1 g TID.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with wife 5 days after discharge. He spent his birthday in the ED: 3 days of confusion and sleepiness, sodium 119, workup fit SIADH from the cancer. Hypertonic saline briefly, then fluid restriction and salt tablets. Sodium 128 on discharge.

Now clear, back to himself, doing crosswords. Sticking to about 5 cups of fluid a day, wife measuring. Salt tabs 1 g three times a day. Lurbinectedin continues every 3 weeks, next dose per oncology.

Exam: alert, oriented x3, conversant. Moist membranes, no edema. Chest unchanged. Heart regular.

BMP today.

A/P
1. SIADH, paraneoplastic. Continue restriction and NaCl tabs. Repeat sodium in 2 weeks. Signs of low sodium reviewed.
2. ES-SCLC on lurbinectedin (oncology).
3. HLD: atorvastatin, aspirin.

documents.title: Sodium result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium is 131 today, up from 128 at discharge. Moving the right way. Keep the fluid limit and salt tablets, and we'll recheck on 12/9. I sent a copy to oncology.

documents.title: Sodium 134
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium 134, nearly normal. Stay on the tablets and the fluid limit through the holidays and we'll look at easing off in the new year.

documents.title: Re: Sodium 134
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thank you. He wants to know if coffee counts in the 5 cups. (It does, I told him.)

events.reason: annual wellness visit and sodium follow-up

conditions.label: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Annual Wellness and Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV plus sodium follow-up. Wife present.

Since Dec: no confusion. Fluid limit kept, salt tablets three times daily. Lurbinectedin every 3 weeks, tolerating it. Morning sputum as always, PEP device most days. No falls.

Meds: atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, NaCl 1 g TID.
PHQ-2 1. Proxy: wife, MOLST on file from oncology.

Vitals as charted, weight 75.5. Exam: thin. Clubbing. Port clean. Crackles at bases, reduced at R base after pleurodesis. Heart regular. No edema. Oriented, speech normal.

BMP yesterday: Na 137.

A/P
1. SIADH, paraneoplastic: resolved for now. Stop salt tablets. Loosen fluid limit to about 1.5 L, recheck sodium with oncology's next labs; any confusion -> call.
2. ES-SCLC on lurbinectedin.
3. Bronchiectasis, asbestosis: stable.
4. HLD: continue statin, aspirin.
RTC in 6 months.

documents.title: Refill: atorvastatin
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Atorvastatin 40 mg 90-day fill, refills remaining on the May 2025 Rx. Pharmacy just confirming. No action needed.

events.reason: shortness of breath, cough, blood-streaked sputum

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 7/4/2026.
68M, ES-SCLC, bronchiectasis, on lurbinectedin. Breathing worse over weeks, productive cough with occasional streaks of blood. No chest pain, no fever. Appetite down, about 5 kg lost in 3 months without trying. Many bouts of bronchitis over the years, never admitted for one. Former smoker 90 pk-yr, quit 2 years ago.
T 36.7, BP 132/84, HR 94, SpO2 94% RA.
Decreased breath sounds and dull to percussion R mid and lower fields. No crackles, no wheeze. Trachea shifted to the R.
CXR: dense R mid/lower zone opacity, mediastinum shifted R.
CT chest: central R bronchial mass with R lung volume loss.
Imp: obstructive atelectasis from central airway tumor.
Oncology paged, will see him this week. Discharged home with wife, return for heavier bleeding or worse breathing.
NKDA.

documents.title: Radiation
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, Bill's wife. After the ER in July the oncologist stopped the lurbinectedin and he's getting radiation to the tumor in the airway, he's about halfway done. They said you got the ER paperwork. We still have him down to see you on September 10, is that still good?

documents.title: Re: Radiation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for writing. Yes, we have the ER note. September 10 is still on and I'll plan extra time. If radiation days make it hard, we can switch it to video. Call us before then for anything.

documents.title: Appointment Confirmed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called wife to confirm 9/10 at 1:30, 40-min slot per PCP. Ride arranged by family. Confirmed.
